name: Incorrect Authorization
principle: The product attempts an authorization check for a resource or action but applies the wrong rule, subject, object, order, or trust boundary. This lets an actor bypass intended access restrictions to read, modify, execute, or consume protected resources.
detection_signals: Java controller/servlet uses request.getParameter("id") or path variable to load/update/delete an object without hasPermission/isOwner/ACL check
authorization decision uses Cookie/Header/request parameter such as role, userId, isAdmin, tenantId directly
code checks only isAuthenticated(), session != null, or login state before privileged read/write/admin action
Spring @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping/@DeleteMapping on sensitive resource lacks @PreAuthorize/@Secured and has no service-layer permission check
SQL SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE uses WHERE id = ? from user input without owner_id/tenant_id/current_user predicate or ACL join
C/C++ request/message handler executes privileged opcode based on client-supplied uid/role without server-side ACL lookup
file/database/resource access occurs before AccessController.checkPermission, Subject.checkPermission, hasRole, or hasPermission call
negative_signals: server-side permission check binds current authenticated principal to target object before access
SQL query constrains resource by both object id and current user/tenant/ACL membership
Spring method has @PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize/@Secured expressing required role and object permission
central authorization filter/interceptor is mapped to all sensitive routes and denies by default
role/user/tenant values are derived from server-side session/security context, not client-controlled fields
object-level owner/ACL check is repeated in service layer before read, update, delete, or execute
false_defense_traps: hiding buttons, links, or pages in client-side UI without server-side checks
checking authentication only and assuming any logged-in user is authorized
RBAC role check without object-level or tenant-level authorization
trusting role/userId/tenantId from cookies, headers, hidden fields, or request parameters
checking authorization before path parsing/canonicalization or before resolving the final resource
verification_focus: Does every protected action authorize the current server-side principal against the exact target resource and operation before access?

consequence_chains.trigger: resource key or object id is user-controlled and not checked against the principal
consequence_chains.consequence: horizontal authorization bypass to read or modify another user's data

consequence_chains.trigger: authorization is performed before parsing, canonicalization, or final resource resolution
consequence_chains.consequence: bypass of access control through alternate path or representation

patch_principle: Enforce deny-by-default server-side authorization on every sensitive endpoint and operation.
Bind checks to business objects: subject, action, resource id, owner, tenant, and ACL/role.
Use vetted authorization frameworks or centralized policy checks, with service-layer enforcement.
Never trust client-supplied role, user, tenant, or privilege fields for authorization.
Canonicalize and resolve the resource before making the authorization decision.
